question: What is the nature of BaSO₄ formed by a reaction of SO₄ SO²⁻₄ and Ba²⁺?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Water insoluble.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• BaSO4 is an **insoluble compound **formed by the reaction of SO42- and Ba2+ ions.
 
• The chemical name of BaSO4 i**s Barium Sulfate.**
 
• It **forms white or colorless crystals that are not soluble in water**.
 
• It is commonly used as a filler in plastics, paints, and other materials due to its inertness and high density.
 
• It is also used in medical imaging as a contrast agent for X-ray and CT scans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
